title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 353 (Liquidator to make returns, etc.)

content.overview: If any Company Liquidator who has made any default in filing, delivering or making any return, account or other document, or in giving any notice which he is by law required to file, deliver, make or give, fails to make good the default within fourteen days after service of a notice requiring him to do so, the Tribunal may, on an application by any contributory or creditor of the company or by the Registrar, make an order directing the Company Liquidator to make good the default within such time as may be specified in the order. Any such order may provide that all costs of and incidental to the application shall be borne by the Company Liquidator.
content.glance: On default in returns/accounts/notices, after 14-day notice, Tribunal may direct the Company Liquidator to make good the default; costs may be borne by the Liquidator.
content.study: Section 353 is the enforcement mechanism for liquidator filing defaults. If a Company Liquidator defaults in any required return, account, document or notice and fails to cure within fourteen days of a notice to do so, the Tribunal may, on application by a contributory, creditor or the Registrar, order him to make good the default within a specified time. The order may cast the costs of the application on the Company Liquidator.

sections.heading: Cure and Tribunal order
sections.body: Default in filing/returns/notices: 14-day cure notice; Tribunal may order compliance; costs may fall on Liquidator.

examples.title: Missed annual statement
examples.body: A Company Liquidator fails to file the s. 348 statement. After a 14-day notice he still does not file. A creditor applies under s. 353 and the Tribunal directs filing within 21 days with costs against the Liquidator.

hypotheticals.question: Who may apply under s. 353?
hypotheticals.analysis: Any contributory or creditor of the company, or the Registrar.

misconceptions.trap: Only the Registrar may enforce liquidator filing defaults.
misconceptions.correction: Contributories and creditors may also apply under s. 353.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 353 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the rule of s. 353. II. Apply to facts. III. Conclude.

examTips: Name s. 353 and its core requirement.
